svg.title: How do we identify each bird in a photo?
svg.desc: SomePhylloscopus imports a photo, detects and crops each bird with YOLO11n detector v4 (whole-image or tiled detection), and extracts both BioCLIP 2 and BioCLIP 2.5 features. The base ID considers 1,343 species. Eligible birds enter a 58-class specialist review (50 leaf warblers and 8 lookalikes), with nearest-neighbor checks for selected groups and fusion of the specialist, Tip-Adapter and GDA scores where applicable. Other predictions use the base candidates and rejection rules. The per-bird report records the detection box, crop, candidate species and model scores.

svg.text: How do we identify each bird in a photo?
Fuse specialist, Tip and GDA scores
Apply rejection rules or mark uncertain
Initial ID and leaf warbler review
The leaf warbler gate selects the route
Review eligible birds and keep the initial prediction in the report
Top base ID is a leaf warbler
Top ID is among 50 trained leaf warblers
If the top ID is outside the group,
the top five contain no leaf warbler,
and the group score is ≤ 0.1, rule out leaf warbler.
Otherwise, mark uncertain and skip review.
a lookalike and keeps the base ID.
Runs when the top ID belongs to a lookalike group
Pale-legged Leaf Warbler · Sakhalin Leaf Warbler
Redistribute scores within the group. One vote per photographer.
If the top ID falls outside these 57 species,
keep the specialist result from the previous step.
Example photo by Frank Vassen · CC BY 2.0 · Cropped with added boxes.
The report uses illustrative candidates and score bars. Model scores and accuracy are distinct.
YOLO locates birds. BioCLIP and specialist review identify species.
